newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco plans bid for 2008 summer Olympic Games.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco plans bid for 2008 summer Olympic Games.

text.p: San Francisco intends to bid for the summer Olympic Games of 2008, joining a long list of other U.S. cities eager to host the games, the local organizing committee said Tuesday.

The Bay Area Sports Organizing Committee has set out to raise $100,000 by May 1 to enter San Francisco into the initial bidding process, according to state Senator Quentin Kopp, an Independent who chairs the committee.
"I've already raised half of it," Kopp said.
A number of American cities, including Cincinnati, Boston, Houston, New York and Seattle, have also expressed interest in hosting the 2008 summer games.

To be considered, bidders must pay a fee of $100,000 to the U.S. Olympic Committee by May 1. If the committee decides to submit a U.S. city for the games, it would review the bids and recommend one of them to the International Olympics Committee, which will make the final selection in 2001.
Kopp said he had already written to 15 major San Francisco area companies, asking them to help the organizing committee raise the $100,000 by May 1.

Kopp said he was "reasonably confident" the committee would raise all of the money in time because local business leaders know that hosting the 2008 games "would be staggeringly beneficial" to the local economy.
Atlanta hosted the 1996 games and the United States also hosted the summer games in Los Angeles in 1984 and the winter games in Lake Placid, New York, in 1980.
